title: Royal Garden audience and lack of radio
summary: Royal Garden was an ordinary nightclub for everyone; radio and television did not exist then.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I mean, in the Oliver days, back in the 1920s, say when Keppert and Oliver and Emmanuel Perez and all of those people played here. If it was just a small group that followed them, or if it was a lot of the whole Chicago public that would come to dance to their music. For instance, say at Royal Garden, was that mostly...
Royal Garden? That was just another nightclub.
Was that mostly for whites or the colored crowd? Oh, no, that was for everybody. Everybody, but... Yeah. People from all over Chicago would go there.
So it wasn't just restricted like a neighborhood place. No, no, no.

Uh-oh. The whole city would go there then at times. Mm-hmm. Of course, in those days they didn't have much radio, naturally no television, so they didn't get a chance to become nationally known. That's it.
That's another thing. See, that's an advantage that the present day outfit has now. The radio and TV, we didn't have that even in my days. No.
